files_reviewed: frontend/src/components/*.tsx and fx/*.tsx (grep for timers, constants, innerHTML)
note: Model calls run only on the server, so there is no ai_browser_call. No database_rules: the app uses server-side SQLite with no client writes. No secret_exposure: env examples have empty key values. Order data and every order action are local mocks behind real-looking flows. Cancel and return run after the customer says yes, with no staff review. Refunds go to a real human approval queue, but approving still moves no money. Tests and the shadcn-style components/ui files were not reviewed. No file was blocked.

labels.what: Mock commerce backend. Orders and customers come from data/orders.json and data/customers.json, with action changes kept in a local SQLite overlay. No store or OMS is called.
cancel_order only patches the local order overlay and returns a refund record. No OMS cancel and no payment void happens.
start_return makes up an RMA id from a UUID and patches the overlay. No return, label or carrier booking is created.
refund only sets status refunded in the overlay, even after a specialist approves it. No payment provider is called.
Reply tells the customer a prepaid label was emailed to their address. No code sends any email.
Approve posts the message 'your refund has been approved, it will appear on your card in 5-10 days' into the customer chat and the console shows a success toast. No money moves.
'Start 14-day trial' links to /demo and 'Talk to sales' links to /console. No trial, signup or sales contact exists.
12 hardcoded demo orders with dates relative to 2026-09-15, used by every agent as live order data.
5 fake customers with names, example.com emails, 555 phone numbers, addresses, tiers and lifetime values, used as the real customer list.
Seed script writes fake conversations, fake CSAT ratings and backdated rows into the real database, and wipes order state and all actions first.
Built-in Test Lab scenarios are seeded at startup and hardcode demo customers and orders (CUST-001, ORD-10350). They fail against a real store.
Landing page plays scripted chats with fixed confidence chips, ticket ids and refund amounts, shown as product output.
Sample storefront page with hardcoded products and prices, signed in as demo customer CUST-001.
Chat request takes customer_id from the client body. Anyone can act as any customer and see their orders, cancel orders or start returns.
Public /api/demo/customers lists every customer with name, email, tier and orders, with no login. The emails also defeat guest email verification.
With no Google client ID and no admin key (the defaults), every console and admin endpoint is open and the caller is treated as admin.
Conversation read, message poll and feedback endpoints have no owner check. The conversation id is the only key.
Embedded chat takes the customer id from the ?customer= URL query, and widget.js passes it from a data-customer-id attribute. No signed token.
Widget tag hardcodes data-customer-id CUST-001, so every visitor is signed in as Maya Chen.
Demo reset-orders needs only the agent role. It restores all orders and deletes the whole actions table, including approval history.
Any agent, not only an admin, can approve a refund of any amount. In open or API-key mode the approver name is free text from the request.
Guest gets full order details and can trigger actions with only an order number and the account email. No code or second factor.
Prompt says never claim a refund, return or cancellation is done. The model's text is sent to the customer with no check for such claims.
Prompt says never invent ticket numbers or response times. No output check strips them.
Prompt says never ask for card numbers, passwords or 2FA codes. Redaction runs only on inbound customer text, not on the model's reply.
Prompt says warranty claim reviews and account recovery need a human. _policy_override has no rule for either, so only the model decides.
Policy text fed to the model says gift cards and other final-sale items cannot be returned. FINAL_SALE_SKUS is defined but never used, so start_return accepts them.
start_return is offered and run on 'yes' with no amount check and no final-sale check. A $1,248 order gets a promised refund with no specialist approval, unlike the refund path.
Confirmation is a start-of-message regex. 'Please don't cancel it' or 'ok wait' counts as yes and runs the cancel or return.
needs_approval only applies to refund. cancel_order releases the full order total with no amount limit.
cancel_order and start_return run when the customer says yes. The customer confirms, but no staff member reviews.
TODAY fixed to 2026-09-15. Return windows, delay checks and refund dates all use it, never the real date.
Return windows (60 and 90 days) and the $5.95 return fee are hardcoded in code and copied as text in the knowledge base.
Policy text says $250 approval limit, but the limit is editable at runtime (0 to 100000). After a change the prompt and the knowledge base give the model two different numbers.
SLA hours hardcoded. SLA_HOURS uses 4 clock hours for high priority while SLA_TEXT tells the customer 4 business hours.
Plan prices and limits hardcoded in UI (349/month, 3 articles, 1 or 10 seats). No backend enforces plans. The 349 price is set again in RoiCalculator.
API URL falls back to http://localhost:8000.
localhost URLs for CORS and the API are baked into the compose file and frontend build.
A real Google OAuth client ID is committed. Client IDs are public by design. The client secret line is empty.
Admin API key stored in localStorage and sent as X-Admin-Key. Any XSS can read it.
Any agent (not only admin) can create or edit knowledge base articles. That text is fed to the model as policy, so an agent can change refund rules.
Copilot rewrite, KB draft and Test Lab run endpoints call the paid model with no rate limit. In default open mode they need no login.
Customer text goes into the model prompt. The only injection guard is a short regex list in signals.py.
/metrics is open when RELAY_METRICS_TOKEN is unset (the default).
Embed iframe posts messages to the parent with target origin '*'.
Conversation ids, which act as bearer tokens for transcripts, are stored in localStorage.
